# Blazor Repo Architect

Let me walk you through Blazor fundamentals and explain your repository architecture.


## What is Blazor?


Blazor is a web framework for building interactive web applications using C# instead of JavaScript. There are several hosting models:

```
Blazor Hosting Models
═════════════════════

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                     │
│  Blazor Server      Blazor WebAssembly (WASM)       │
│  ─────────────      ─────────────────────────       │
│                                                     │
│  ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐                     │
│  │ Browser │        │ Browser │                     │
│  │  (UI)   │        │ (C# +   │                     │
│  └────┬────┘        │  .NET)  │                     │
│       │SignalR      └─────────┘                     │
│       │                                             │
│  ┌────▼────┐        Everything runs                 │
│  │ Server  │        in browser via                  │
│  │ (.NET)  │        WebAssembly                     │
│  └─────────┘                                        │
│                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         Blazor Web App (Hybrid - .NET 8+)
         ────────────────────────────────
         Can mix Server + WASM + Static SSR
```

Your app uses **Blazor Web App** template (the modern approach in .NET 8+), which supports multiple rendering modes.


## Repository Architecture Explained


Let me break down each part:

```
blazor-basic/
│
├── Program.cs                    ← App entry point (like Main in console apps)
├── appsettings.json             ← Configuration (connection strings, API keys)
├── appsettings.Development.json ← Dev-specific config (overrides appsettings.json)
│
├── blazor-basic.csproj          ← Project file (dependencies, SDK version)
├── blazor-basic.sln             ← Solution file (can contain multiple projects)
│
├── Components/                   ← Your Blazor components (pages, layouts)
│   ├── App.razor                ← Root component (HTML head, body)
│   ├── Routes.razor             ← Routing configuration
│   ├── _Imports.razor           ← Global using statements for components
│   │
│   ├── Pages/                   ← Routable pages (@page directive)
│   │   ├── Home.razor          ← Default page at "/"
│   │   ├── Counter.razor       ← Demo page at "/counter"
│   │   └── Weather.razor       ← Demo page at "/weather"
│   │
│   └── Layout/                  ← Layout components
│       ├── MainLayout.razor    ← Main app layout wrapper
│       └── NavMenu.razor       ← Navigation menu
│
├── wwwroot/                     ← Static files (CSS, JS, images)
│   ├── app.css                 ← Global styles
│   ├── favicon.png             ← Browser icon
│   └── lib/                    ← Client-side libraries (Bootstrap, etc.)
│
├── Properties/
│   └── launchSettings.json     ← Debug profiles, ports, SSL settings
│
├── bin/                         ← Compiled output (don't commit to Git)
└── obj/                         ← Build intermediates (don't commit to Git)
```


## Key Files Deep Dive


### **Program.cs** - The Starting Point

```
Request Flow
════════════

HTTP Request → Program.cs → Middleware Pipeline → Router → Component
                    │
                    ├─ Add Services (DI)
                    ├─ Configure Pipeline
                    └─ Map Routes
```

Typical structure:
```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Add services to DI container
builder.Services.AddRazorComponents()
    .AddInteractiveServerComponents();  // Enable server-side interactivity

var app = builder.Build();

// Configure HTTP request pipeline
app.UseStaticFiles();      // Serve wwwroot files
app.UseAntiforgery();      // CSRF protection
app.MapRazorComponents<App>()
    .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode();  // Enable @rendermode

app.Run();
```


### **Components/App.razor** - Root Component

Think of this as your HTML document structure:

```razor
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <HeadOutlet />  <!-- Dynamic head content -->
</head>
<body>
    <Routes />      <!-- Where your pages render -->
    <script src="_framework/blazor.web.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
```


### **Components/Routes.razor** - Router Configuration

```razor
<Router AppAssembly="@typeof(Program).Assembly">
    <Found Context="routeData">
        <RouteView RouteData="@routeData" DefaultLayout="@typeof(Layout.MainLayout)" />
    </Found>
    <NotFound>
        <h1>404 - Page not found</h1>
    </NotFound>
</Router>
```

```
Router Logic
════════════

URL: /counter
    │
    ├─ Search for @page "/counter"
    │
    ├─ Found: Counter.razor
    │
    ├─ Wrap in MainLayout
    │
    └─ Render to Browser
```


## Component Structure


A typical Blazor component (.razor file):

```razor
@page "/example"           <!-- 1. Route (optional) -->
@using System.Net.Http     <!-- 2. Using statements (or in _Imports.razor) -->
@inject HttpClient Http    <!-- 3. Dependency Injection -->

<!-- 4. HTML Markup with C# -->
<h3>Hello, @name!</h3>
<button @onclick="HandleClick">Click me</button>

@code {                    <!-- 5. C# Code Block -->
    private string name = "World";
    
    private void HandleClick()
    {
        name = "Blazor";
    }
}
```


## Component Lifecycle


```
Component Lifecycle
═══════════════════

Initialize
    │
    ├─ SetParametersAsync()      ← Parameters received
    │
    ├─ OnInitialized()            ← Component created
    │   OnInitializedAsync()      
    │
    ├─ OnParametersSet()          ← After parameters set
    │   OnParametersSetAsync()    
    │
    ├─ BuildRenderTree()          ← Generate UI
    │
    └─ OnAfterRender()            ← After browser renders
        OnAfterRenderAsync()      

Update (when state changes)
    │
    ├─ OnParametersSet()
    ├─ BuildRenderTree()
    └─ OnAfterRender()

Dispose
    │
    └─ Dispose() / DisposeAsync()
```


## Rendering Modes (.NET 8+)


Your app can use different rendering strategies:

```razor
@* Static Server-Side Rendering (SSR) - No interactivity *@
<Counter />

@* Interactive Server - Real-time via SignalR *@
<Counter @rendermode="InteractiveServer" />

@* Interactive WebAssembly - Runs in browser *@
<Counter @rendermode="InteractiveWebAssembly" />

@* Interactive Auto - Server first, then WASM *@
<Counter @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
```


## Data Flow Pattern


```
Parent-Child Data Flow
══════════════════════

┌─────────────────────────────┐
│   Parent Component          │
│                             │
│   [Parameter]               │
│   public string Title       │
│                             │
│   [EventCallback]           │
│   OnChildEvent()            │
│         ▲                   │
│         │ Event             │
└─────────┼───────────────────┘
          │
          │ Parameter
          ▼
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│   Child Component           │
│                             │
│   [Parameter]               │
│   public string Title       │
│                             │
│   InvokeAsync(OnChildEvent) │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```


## Dependency Injection Example


In `Program.cs`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddScoped<IWeatherService, WeatherService>();
```

In your component:

```razor
@inject IWeatherService WeatherService

@code {
    private WeatherForecast[]? forecasts;
    
    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        forecasts = await WeatherService.GetForecastAsync();
    }
}
```


## Common Service Lifetimes


```
Service Lifetimes
═════════════════

Transient
    ├─ New instance every time
    └─ AddTransient<T>()

Scoped
    ├─ One instance per request/circuit
    └─ AddScoped<T>()        ← Most common for Blazor Server

Singleton
    ├─ One instance for app lifetime
    └─ AddSingleton<T>()
```
